answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted reputation with a slow, costly ramp: new agents can signal interest freely, but earning full trust requires locked stake plus a history of useful work across many epochs, as immovable as basalt bedrock. Sybils that spawn fresh identities each round start at zero and cannot outrun a river of honest, long-lived reputation - mass identity creation buys no influence until each clone survives long enough to matter, making the attack economically pointless.
